mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is at or below 0.2%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to reduced cost of capital for equity financing and increased risk appetite for equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) exceeding 520.0 thousand units signals robust consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as companies benefit from higher sales and profit margins.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST > 520.0.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market characterized by payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 130,000 thousand and unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 10.0% signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000 and UNRATE < 10.0.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of robust industrial output (INDPRO > 95.0), the S&P 500 generates positive 20-day forward returns as manufacturing sector strength translates to broader equity market gains.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 219.0 signals high inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors demand higher risk premiums.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 219.0.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales level (RSAFS) exceeding 378,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher corporate revenue expectations and profit growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS > 378000.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%) and high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL > 219.0) signals inflationary pressures that erode real equity returns, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as central banks may delay rate cuts.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.2 and CPIAUCSL > 219.0.

mechanism_narrative: In the high industrial production regime (INDPRO > 95.0), the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day forward returns as manufacturing momentum quickly translates to equity market gains due to short-term earnings momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 95.0.
